chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Isma'il ibn Jabir and Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, “What do you think about the martyr—should he be buried with his blood?” He said, “Yes, in his clothes, with his blood. He is not perfumed with hanut, he is not washed, and he is buried as he is.”

Then he said, “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله buried his uncle Hamzah in his clothes, with the blood in which he had been struck. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله added a mantle for him, but it fell short of covering his feet, so he called for idhkhir and cast it over him. And he offered seventy prayers over him and pronounced seventy takbirs over him.”

key_terms.الشَّهِيدَ: the martyr; one killed in the path of Allah whose burial has special rulings
key_terms.بُرْدًا: a mantle or cloak placed over the deceased
key_terms.بِدِمَائِهِ: with his blood; meaning he is buried without removing the traces of martyrdom
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةً: a pronouncement of 'Allahu akbar' in the funeral prayer
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: to be perfumed with hanut; a funerary perfume applied to the deceased
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: to be washed with ghusl; the ritual washing of the dead

ai.seo_question: How should a martyr be buried according to the hadith of Abi Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling that the martyr is buried in his own blood-stained clothes without ghusl or hanut. It supports this ruling by citing the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in the burial of Hamzah, showing the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding martyrs.
